cohort: The study included 120 subjects admitted to a hospital between January 1, 2016, and January 1, 2018, divided into an observation group of 60 pregnant women with hepatitis B infection and a control group of 60 healthy pregnant women.
finding: Pregnancy complicated with hepatitis B infection significantly increased the incidence rates of premature rupture of fetal membranes, premature delivery, postpartum hemorrhage, pregnancy-induced hypertension syndrome, neonatal distress, and neonatal asphyxia, and influenced neonatal immunological factors (CD3(+), CD4(+), CD19(+), IgA, IgM) in umbilical cord blood.
mod_finding: No significant differences were identified in the incidence rate of cesarean delivery between the observation and control groups.
followup_time: Observations were taken related to pregnancy outcomes and neonatal complications, implying immediate post-birth assessment (e.g., umbilical cord blood, neonatal complications at birth).
